text.p: The merger of Allegheny Power System Inc and DQE Inc will result in cost savings of $1 billion over the next ten years, officials from both energy companies said Monday.
"There are a number of areas that (savings) are coming from. Labor is certainly one large area," Alan J. Noia, president and chief executive of Allegheny Power, said at a news conference.

"The combined 11,000 megawatts of generating capacity will now be able to dispatched more economically than each of us could have done on our own," Noia added. "So there are these natural synergies. DQE peaks in the summertime, we peak in the wintertime. All of these things combined produce that $1 billion in savings."
Noia and David D. Marshall, president and chief executive of DQE, also said about 500 jobs will be lost as a result of the merger. The job cuts will be spread across both companies.
The workforce reductions will be achieved through attrition and early retirements. Noia said the combined workforce after the merger will be about 8,500.
The executives also said rates will not go up as a result of the merger, and are likely to decrease.
"You will see rates from both companies being lower than they would otherwise be on a stand-alone basis," Marshall said.
The two companies announced early Monday that they would merge in a deal valued at approximately $10.6 billion.
Under terms of the transaction, DQE shareholders will receive 1.12 shares of Allegheny Power common stock for each share of DQE common stock.
The companies said in a news release they hope to obtain all required approvals within 12 to 18 months.
Allegheny Power provides electricity to nearly 1.4 million customers in parts of Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia.
DQE's subsidiary, Duquesne Light Co, serves more than 580,000 customers in a service territory that is approximately 800 square miles, including the city of Pittsburgh.
